To: All Head Office Staff

Subject: Student Visit Week, March 23-27
Dear Colleagues,
Last year's Student Visit Week was well received by the students from Dunmore Technical College and by the employees who took part, and the college has asked to send a second group in March. Fourteen students will attend, and one host is needed for each. This program is separate from the in-house Supervisor Skills course, which continues as scheduled.
The students will be on site from 9:30 A.M. until 3:30 P.M. each day. Passes will be issued at the sign-in counter on the ground floor on Monday morning, and hosts should meet their assigned student there before going up to the team work areas. Hosts will receive a short briefing in the third-floor training room the previous Thursday, and one midday meal in the staff dining area is provided. Every host is also asked to write a few lines at the end of each day, and these notes will shape the plan for next year's group.
Staff who wish to take part can choose from three levels of commitment. A full-week host keeps one student from Monday to Friday and sets a task each morning. A two-day host shares one student with a second host on any two days, while a single-day host takes one student for just one day. Please note that no more than three hosts per team can be accepted.
To take part, send me a short message stating which option you have chosen, no later than Friday, March 6. Your team leader's agreement must already be in place, as that cannot be arranged through this office.
Thank you for your help.
Joyce Tanaka
Learning Programs Coordinator
Internal extension 418

Frances Duvall, who opened Renshaw Stationers and has directed it ever since, will step back from daily management at the end of this month. Two members of her staff, Grace Abbott and Emil Kovacs, will take on the business jointly from June 1.

Orders may be placed by e-mail throughout the closure, with no charge added for delivery. Deliveries themselves begin again on the reopening day, and a customer who needs an order before then may pick it up from the company's storage unit on Kestrel Lane.

Annual Comparison
Small-Office Copiers: How This Year's Ratings Were Made
Four submitted units, one rating still unfinished.
By our equipment testing editor, Naomi Pilcher
Four criteria decide the standing. Running cost per page carries the greatest weight, followed by output quality, then speed, then reliability in daily use. Last year speed came first, but readers told us that running costs matter more, so the order was changed for this cycle. Each criterion is placed in one of three bands, excellent, good, or fair, and the standard program runs ten weeks.
The LP-620 reached our test office eleven days after the testing period had closed, leaving no time to measure its running cost before we went to press. Under our standing rule, a unit that completes only part of the program is published with a provisional standing and may be rated again if its maker returns it.
The full grid appears opposite.
Test samples are bought at ordinary retail prices by this magazine unless the grid states otherwise.
----------------------
This Year's Ratings: Small-Office Copiers
Criterion	TN-415	ZR-88	VC-350	LP-620
Running cost per page	Good	Good	Excellent	Not rated
Output quality	Excellent	Good	Good	Excellent
Speed	Good	Excellent	Fair	Good
Reliability in daily use	Excellent	Good	Excellent	Good
Overall standing	2nd	3rd	1st	4th
Test sample	Retail purchase	Maker's demonstration unit	Retail purchase	Retail purchase
Weeks in test	10	10	4	3
Status	Full rating	Full rating	Full rating, short run only	Provisional, running cost not measured
----------------------
Following our small-office copier comparison in the March issue
Readers Ask
The maker of the LP-620 sent it back to you. Has its place in the grid changed? — from an office administrator
It has. The unit ran the complete program in April, and its running cost was measured for the first time, falling in the middle band. With all four criteria scored, the provisional entry is withdrawn, and the LP-620 now stands third, ahead of the ZR-88.
We copy customer documents all day, and running cost is not our concern. Where in the grid should we look? — from a print-room supervisor
Do not start with the standing row, which is led by the unit that is cheapest to run. Choose the model that took the top band for output quality and also for reliability in daily use, and that stayed in the test the full ten weeks.
— N. Pilcher, Equipment Testing Editor
Send further questions to our testing desk.
